title: Dimension of fibres of a morphism of locally algebraic schemes: bounds, openness and the generic value
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For a morphism f: X to Y of locally algebraic k-schemes, the lemma records that fibres are locally algebraic over the residue field, and for X irreducible with Z the closure of the image and d = dim(X) - dim(Z), it bounds the fibre dimension below by d, asserts that equality holds on a dense open, gives an upper bound in terms of the dimension of the local ring of Z at f(x), and identifies the fibre dimension with d when that local ring has dimension one; a final part bounds the fibre dimension at an arbitrary point by dim_x(X) - dim_y(Y) (statement lines 3952-3972). The proof first computes d as a transcendence degree of the extension of the function field of Z inside the function field of X at the generic point, which identifies d with the fibre dimension at the generic point of X (proof lines 3983-3990). The lower bound and the density of equality are then the openness of bounded fibre dimension, and the two refined bounds come from the codimension one and higher codimension lemmas of the same chapter (proof lines 3991-3995). The last part reduces to an irreducible component of X through x of dimension dim_x(X) and applies the irreducible case to it (proof lines 3998-4000). The claim is H2: one transcendence degree computation plus a careful routing of four statements to the appropriate earlier results.
